root_cause.text: The x86 kexec relocation code stopped placing a dummy return address on the purgatory stack in the non-`preserve_context` path, but `kexec-tools` purgatory unconditionally reads the word above the stack as a kjump return address, so the missing stack word caused an out-of-bounds access/fault.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `pushq $0` in `arch/x86/kernel/relocate_kernel_64.S` with the comment that purgatory “will unconditionally look for the return address on the stack,” and the commit message says the prior fix “no longer ‘gratuitously’ pushes the unused return address to the stack in the non-kjump path,” which made “the word above the stack might not be there, leading to a fault.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Force a zero return address onto the stack for normal kexec so purgatory does not misidentify it as a preserve-context jump-back operation.
intent_record.what: A new `pushq $0` instruction was inserted before the existing `pushq %rdx` in the `identity_mapped` code path, along with a comment explaining that the return address should be forced to zero when context is not being preserved.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this places a zero value on the stack ahead of the start address, ensuring the purgatory code in kexec-tools sees a non-preserve-context kexec as having no return address and therefore does not set `kexec_jump_back_entry=`. This changes the stack layout used for the handoff and distinguishes normal kexec from kjump preserve-context behavior.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it restores a dummy/zero return address on the purgatory stack for the non-preserve_context path, preventing purgatory from reading an invalid missing stack word and faulting.

candidates.rationale: This pre-fix stack setup only pushed the start address and did not place a dummy zero return address above it. As a result, purgatory later read an unexpected/missing word above the stack and could treat normal kexec as a preserve-context jump-back, triggering the out-of-bounds access/fault.

vuln_statements.explanation: This pre-fix stack setup only pushed the start address and did not place a dummy zero return address above it. In the non-preserve_context path, purgatory later expects to read a kjump return address from the word above the stack, so omitting this extra stack word caused the out-of-bounds access/fault.
